Been playing GW2 on and off for years in standalone. Many start-overs as a f2p player up until very recently with buying HoT & PoF expansions.

The core free-to-play value of GW2 is plentiful and then some. I suggest playing until you get to level 80 and/or then deciding whether or not you want to invest money into the game. There is a lot to learn, don't be like me and excessively create and delete characters. Decide in advance 2 classes you want to try and grind em till you make up your mind.

Well worth it in my opinion, GW2 has given me 100's of hours of enjoyment before even spending a dime and that makes it well worth buying expansion(s) IMO.

Don't rush to 80 or end-game, enjoy the journey!

I've got hundreds of hours in GW2 way before the Steam release. It's the best MMORPG out there in my opinion.
It's just easy. That's what makes it fun, what most MMO's lack. No I don't want to do a 30 minute fetch quest where 28 minutes of it is walking there and back. Guild Wars 2 eliminates that. You just go to an area / region and complete whatever quest you want, in whatever order you want and it all goes into a "region completion" bar. There is a story line but it's also simple and marked on the map, and you can choose to do them or not, you can choose not to and just complete regions if that's what you want. It's just a lot of player control, it doesn't feel like a chore.

If you want an MMO that is easy to understand, relaxed and lets you go at your own pace then GW2 is the MMO for you. Simple as.

Helpful sites for new (and old) players:

• wiki.guildwars2.com – one of the strengths of Guild Wars 2 is its wiki. From lore to gameplay, every part of the game is explained with guides and helpful visuals.
• en-forum.guildwars2.com – the Guild Wars 2 forums.
• guildjen.com – guides, builds, and updates about the game.
• gw2crafts.net – a helpful site to optimally level up your different crafting disciplines.
• www.metabattle.com – simple builds for every class and for every game type.
• www.snowcrows.com – meta builds for raids and fractals, which are the endgame content.
• www.godsofpvp.net – builds and guides for PvP.
• www.hardstuck.gg/gw2/builds – more builds
• gw2mists.com – builds and guides for the World vs World game content.
• gw2efficiency.com – a useful tool for any player.

I've been playing this game on and off for about eight of its ten years, and I absolutely love it.

Everything that GW2 does that other MMOs do, it either did first, or it does better.

For example, the mounts are all fabulously unique. Where other games' mounts are simply a gold tax to move faster, GW2's mounts all provide unique movement modes to change how you travel.

The community is friendly, and always goes out of their way to be helpful.

Here's to ten more years!

Support responds quickly, which is a lot more than I can say about some companies.
Premium currency can be exchanged for gold, or vice versa. (Yay no gold seller spam, gj ArenaNet)

I don't really have anything in the cons, except that some features are locked behind the purchase of an expansion, but that is kind of expected in any f2p game. They aren't really necessary but I picked one up anyways.

Is it fun? Yes.....Yes it is. Will you know what your doing for the first few hours? Nope.....not at all.
But if you manage to stick with it and maybe take some time to learn the ropes, its a pretty good time consumer you can sink a lot of time into.

You know that feeling you got when you were a kid playing games on the family desktop? You never wanted to stop and looked forward to it when you had other things to do... This is giving that feeling.

A friend recommended it to me, so I gave it a try... and I’m glad I did. I was expecting the usual MMO grind, but it’s surprisingly easy to just log in, explore, and have fun without feeling pressured.

You can wander into events, help out, grab some loot, and suddenly you’ve made solid progress without even realizing it. Combat keeps you awake, stand in a red circle and you’ll regret it. Movement matters, dodging matters, and fights feel active instead of “press 1 and wait.”

The world feels alive, random players naturally group up during events, and everyone gets credit so there’s no weird competition over kills.

Didn’t expect much going in, but it’s been a really enjoyable experience so far.
